subject: Latency slotting & metrics definitions for hosted API — clarifications
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Cole <avery.cole@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency slotting & metrics definitions for hosted API — clarifications

Hey Avery,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I'm putting together a short proposal for how Redwood would operationalize p50/p95 commitments for your hosted API usage and wanted to confirm a few things before we lock numbers into the term sheet. Attaching a concise PDF and our raw latency matrix for reference.

Quick context of what we mean by "slotting": we propose defining 3 latency slots ("Interactive", "Background", "Bulk") that map to typical request shapes you described. Each slot has a separate p50/p95 target and measurement window so we avoid an aggregate SLO masking tail behavior during sporadic bulk jobs.

High-level asks from your side so we align the legal language and the contract carveouts:
- Confirm which traffic classes you consider "Interactive" vs "Background" vs "Bulk" (we can map by route or by header).
- Are there planned batch windows that should be carved out for measurement?
- Is cross-region failover allowed or must all traffic stay in us-east-1?

Proposed starting targets (draft):
- Interactive slot: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 220ms measured on a 5-minute rolling window (primary measurement).
- Background slot: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms measured on an hourly window.
- Bulk slot: p50 <= 400ms, p95 <= 1.2s measured on a 3-hour window with explicit burst carveouts.

Notes: these are engineering-driven starting points designed to balance cost and perceived latency. We’ll include a fallback policy (route to small-context model with a documented fidelity delta) and automated KV-cache seeding to reduce p95 noise for repeat prefixes.

Could you confirm the three bullet items above and attach your procurement/legal contact so Laura can start drafting the contract language?

Thanks,
Connor
---
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Avery Cole <avery.cole@vectorhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivers <trivers@vectorhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency slotting & metrics definitions for hosted API — clarifications

Connor —

Appreciate the write-up. This is already more useful than the spreadsheet we had internally. Quick answers inline:

- Traffic classification: Interactive = API routes that drive UI interactions (mostly /chat and /completions for user sessions). Background = async enrichment jobs and webhook-driven scoring. Bulk = nightly batch embedding jobs and large ingestion pipelines. We'll provide a list of route prefixes by EOD.
- Batch windows: Yes — we run major backfill jobs between 02:00-05:00 local on weekdays in our us-east-1 region. We'd like those excluded from p95 measurement for Bulk slot as they inflate our tail.
- Cross-region: We prefer primary processing to stay in us-east-1 for data locality and compliance. Failover to us-west-2 is allowed but only for emergency (we'll require documented failover events to be excluded from SLO calculation).

A couple of follow-ups from Tom:
1) What exactly do you mean by "automated KV-cache seeding" and will that be enabled by default?
2) For the fallback small-context model, can you quantify the fidelity delta and whether that will count as a separate model catalog entry (we prefer explicit model labels in telemetry).

I'll loop in Procurement shortly — procurement@vectorhealth.com — please include Laura on the contract thread.

Thanks,
Avery

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Cole <avery.cole@vectorhealth.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency slotting & metrics definitions for hosted API — clarifications

Thanks for the quick clarifications, Avery. Looping in Ben to answer the technical pieces and Laura for contract next steps.

Ben — short technical responses below; happy to jump on a quick 30-minute call if you want to dig into telemetry math.

- KV-cache seeding: We pre-warm prefix-level Key-Value cache for frequently accessed conversational sessions. Enabled by default for Interactive slot; configurable per-customer. It reduces first-request variance for warmed prefixes and will improve p95 for interactive conversational workloads where users send many incremental messages. The seeding behavior is visible in trace spans and is controllable via a customer config.
- Fallback model fidelity: The fallback is a quantized smaller-parameter variant in the Redwood catalog (we tag it e.g., redwood-compact-v1). Typical measured fidelity delta on our benchmarks is ~2–4 ROUGE-like points depending on prompt shape; for scalar scoring tasks the delta is often <1%. We will always surface which model served each request in telemetry so you can filter SLOs by model if needed.

Action items:
- VectorHealth: send route prefix list and confirm the list of producers for batch jobs.
- Redwood: Ben will propose a concrete measurement windowing clause and a transparent failover carveout definition; Laura will draft the initial clause for procurement.

Connor

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Avery Cole <avery.cole@vectorhealth.com>, Tom Rivers <trivers@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency slotting & metrics definitions for hosted API — clarifications

Hi all —

Following up with a draft of the measurement language we recommend for the contract. I kept it intentionally concrete so legal can copy/paste. Feedback welcome.

Proposed measurement clause (draft):
- Measurement windows: 
  * Interactive: p50/p95 computed from a 5-minute rolling window, computed every minute, with retention of 90 days of raw latency samples.
  * Background: p50/p95 computed from a 1-hour rolling window, sampled every 5 minutes.
  * Bulk: p50/p95 computed from a 3-hour rolling window, sampled every 15 minutes with an explicit batch-job carveout period defined by customer-provided job schedule.
- Carveouts and Failover: documented cross-region failovers and customer-declared maintenance windows will be excluded from SLO calculations if notified within 48 hours of the event; automatic autoscaling events are not carveouts.
- Model-labeling: all responses will include a model_label field; SLOs will apply to the route-slot mapping irrespective of model_label unless otherwise specified by customer.
- Transparency: Redwood will provide a daily SLO digest and a raw telemetry export (CSV) on request for audit.

Notes:
- Sampling cadence and rolling window choices aim to avoid overfitting to one-off microbursts while preserving meaningful SLA enforcement.
- We recommend starting with the windows above for the first 90-day commitment cycle and revisiting after the initial month of telemetry.

Attachments: redwood-latency-slotting-proposal-v1.pdf (contains example graphs and sample CSV slice).

Ben Carter
Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Ben/Connor —

This all looks reasonable and matches our internal thinking. A couple of small contract asks before we sign:

- We need the ability to flag a scheduled batch-window as a recurring carveout (nightly 02:00-05:00 ET) rather than manually notifying each time.
- For emergency cross-region failover exclusions, we'd like a cap of 6 events per 12-month period that can be auto-excluded; additional events would require joint review.
- Please include the CSV telemetry export format as an appendix so our SREs can ingest directly into Grafana.

If you can update the draft clause with those three points (recurring carveout, 6-event cap, CSV schema appendix) we can route to Procurement and Legal and aim to sign early next week.

Tom
